Exploits core.fsmonitor Git configuration setting
Executes arbitrary commands at user privilege level
Four flaws unpatched as of September 1, 2026

Malicious Apache modules redirect to fake app store phishing pages
At least 20 .gov.br portals (municipalities and police forces) compromised

nvidia-leads-chip-stocks-higher-on-renew.one_liner: Nvidia and semiconductor stocks rallied as investor confidence in sustained AI spending strengthened.

ai-designed-proteins-improve-rna-deliver.one_liner: Researchers developed AI-designed proteins that function as RNA transporters, enabling delivery of RNA therapeutics into cells for gene-modifying treatments.

pacman-ai-framework-enables-millisecond-.one_liner: Researchers at Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory developed PACMAN, an AI framework that makes critical fusion system control decisions in milliseconds faster than human operators.

un-report-global-warming-will-exceed-15c.title: UN Report: Global Warming Will Exceed 1.5°C Paris Agreement Target
un-report-global-warming-will-exceed-15c.one_liner: A UN report projects that global temperatures will surpass the 1.5°C warming limit set by the Paris Agreement, shifting climate strategy to minimizing time above the threshold.

google-avoids-ad-business-breakup-but-fa.title: Google avoids ad-business breakup but faces operational restrictions from court
google-avoids-ad-business-breakup-but-fa.one_liner: A federal judge rejected the Department of Justice's proposal to break up Google's ad-technology business on September 2, 2026, but ordered the company to adjust its practices to create competitive advantages for rivals. The ruling followed an April 2025 finding that Google had acted illegally in maintaining its ad-tech dominance.
takeaways: Judge Leonie M. Brinkema rejected DOJ breakup proposal
Google must modify business practices to favor competitors
Specific operational changes not detailed in initial ruling
Ruling sealed for 14 days pending redactions
Follows separate 2025 search-business antitrust ruling by Judge Amit Mehta
